global.note: Variables kept in the catalogue but never attached to an event. `*` applies to every module; a module key applies to that module only, which is how the session keeps its own `main_location` (the hearing link or the court it is held in) while every other module drops the record URL. Free-text bodies (remarks, request content, hearing minutes, descriptions, the statement question and its response) are never notification variables: a notification carries the record’s identity, its people and its dates, not a paragraph the user typed. A contract only fills the detail table of its own type, so the per-type fields are dropped as well and contracts expose the fields every type shares. A cause request drops its reviewer: `reviewer_id` is never written by the stage actions the request actually goes through, so the field printed an empty line in every message that named it.

create_cause_request.note: A form that is only now being added to the cause has never left a stage, so it has no previous one to report.

create_cause.note: No actor is attached while the cause is being created; the designated employee and the team are assigned by a later action. A brand new cause carries no sub status either.

close_cause.note: Closing or reopening a cause only announces the record's identity, its dates, its court/department and who created it — the people working it (assigner, team), the parties, and the internal status/sub_status are noise on this notification, so only the logical fields are kept.

reopen_cause.note: Same logical field set as close_cause: identity, dates, court/department and creator only.

create_cause_session.note: The adjournment note is written when the session is adjusted, never while it is being created. The competent employee of the session is only stamped then too: at creation assigner_id is copied from the cause, so it names the cause's employee rather than the one who will attend the hearing.

create_cause_judgment.note: The receiving date is only stamped by the "receive judgment" action.

create_help_request.note: The statement has no answer until it is answered. The legacy `answer` column is never written; answers live in the answers relation.

answer_help_request.note: The legacy `answer` column is never written; the answer text comes from the answers relation.

assign_department_consultation.note: Only the department is set at this point; employees are assigned later and no draft exists yet.

assign_users_consultation.note: The employees are just being assigned; the draft is written afterwards.

create_draft_consultation.note: The draft reviewer is only recorded when the draft is approved.

return_draft_to_employee_consultation.note: The draft is sent back for rework, so it has no reviewer yet.
